text: If I eat more than 100g of protein per day I tend to feel constantly unsatisfied (not exactly hungry, just unsatisfied), bloated, low energy, and my weight creeps up. If I stay in the 70-90g zone with higher fat (60-70ish g) and higher carbs (about 180-200), I feel satisfied, energetic, and no bloat. All my clothes fit and I drop a few pounds eating more calories. I’ve tried to eat higher protein for years. More than 100g a day just does not work for me and I am so much happier and lighter keeping protein moderate.
label: experience

text:
Contrary to your experience, my bloating has reduced since going on a high protein diet. I tend to retain water because of carbs. I get very puffy in the face, my stomach also bulges on a carb heavy diet. I’ve noticed my weight go up by a few kgs whenever I have a carb heavy day.

Another thing that I noticed is my acne gets better when I have more whey and eggs. I know whey tends to give acne to a lot of people. Certain brands gave me severe breakout after just one scoop. But the brands that work for me, they really helped control my acne. It could also be that when I have protein heavy meals, I have less carbs, more fats, so that helps reduce breakouts as well.

My muscles have more definition since going on high protein diet. Especially hamstrings. I was one of those people with naturally flat thighs in the back. No matter how much I workout, they never had that toned, bulgy look. High protein definitely built all those muscles. I have rounded thighs now.

My hair got better, energy levels are high, I feel lighter and in better mood overall. It’s also that I significantly increased my fibre intake since going on high protein diet. More fibre also makes me feel lighter and energetic compared to carbs.

Downside - I see only one. I come from a culture where breads and rice are a staple with every meal. My body still doesn’t feel full unless I have some type of carb in every meal. I get extremely hungry if I only have protein and fats. Also, carbs help me sleep better. Protein alone isn’t able to do that.
label: experience

text:
I'm about six weeks in. I have PCOS and have lost about 17 lbs so far. Arthritis pain is 90% reduced. Much less intestinal distress. I can now view food as fuel and not a hobby.

The biggest difference is energy and motivation. I wouldn't say I was low energy before, but I would come home from work, eat dinner, and then sit on the couch for a while scrolling Reddit or whatever. I had to force myself to get up and do something, or else I would end up taking a nap. I would try to make myself go for a walk or something, but I always felt like there weren't enough hours to be able to spend an hour walking and get everything else done.

Now I feel like there are way more hours in the day. I wake up earlier, actually getting less sleep but feeling more rested. Like seriously, who is this person that gets up at 7:30 am on a Saturday and goes out and runs errands in the morning? I could never drag myself out of bed before 10:00 am before. Now when I get home from work I go for an hour long walk, make dinner, make my lunch for the next day, clean the kitchen, do chores/laundry, practice my instrument. I have no desire to sit on the couch and watch TV. I am actively looking for more things to be involved in because I have too much time to fill now.
label: experience

text: Benefit: I thought at first that keto would feel restrictive but it actually feels streamlined. The amount of food decisions I have to make in a day is so much smaller. When trying to eat healthy before there was so much possible choice that it made planning meals a huge to-do. You'd wind up with extremely varied groceries, things you'd use half of and then waste, having to decide between a huge list of possibilities for every piece of every meal. Knowing that there is a limited set of things you choose to eat on a regular basis makes shopping, planning, and cooking really simplified. Added benefit that because my meals all fit a very similar blueprint, I don't usually feel the need to track anything - even my carbs - unless I eat at a restaurant or have an unexpected meal type.
label: experience

text:
I've been eating keto since November 2017. I’ve experienced no drawbacks, only benefits.

I've lost 80lbs (I haven't been this this since I graduated high school in 2004) and keto keeps my appetite under control well enough that I’ve maintained my weight loss. This is a huge deal as I am a recovering binge eater.

My chronic insomnia and acid reflux are totally gone.

I regulated my blood pressure and I've greatly improved and perfected my cholesterol and triglyceride numbers since they were through the roof pre-keto.

My menstrual cycle has normalized (it is lighter, less painful, and predictable to the day for the first time in my life).

My anxiety has lessened considerably and I am now able to maintain my calm/cool/collected was in situations that previously would’ve sent me spiraling.

My libido is always off the charts now, which is amazing.

I've seen serious improvement in my overall dental health (my dentist is very pleased!).

I've gotten rid of the constant brain fog I was unaware existed...mental clarity is a gift I will never take for granted again.

I found a renewed happiness with my life, and self-confidence I never thought I'd get back. I've let go of a serious food/sugar addiction I didn't even realize I had; food was controlling my life and I've taken that control back. It's liberating to not be a slave to the cravings, life changing in many ways for someone like me. :)
label: experience

text:
Throughout 6 years long of extreme starvation and malnutrition, my diet mainly consisted of protein.

I barely ever got sick (probably once in 2 years), i was still able to walk and run normally, never ever fainted, and my heart somehow never gave up (heart health was a major problem). Doctors told me that I'd survive 2 years maximum before my body would give up, it didn't. I'm actually pretty sure that it was because my choice of caloric intake only went to protein. It wasn't the healthiest lifestyle I know, but protein might've actually saved my life.

That aside, magnesium!!! Was struggling with a lot of muscle tension, and the reason I started taking magnesium is for entirely different reasons... But never had any muscle tension again since I've been taking magnesium.
